newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ISRAEL'S PERES SAYS PEACE WILL NOT BE HALTED.
newsitem.headline: ISRAEL'S PERES SAYS PEACE WILL NOT BE HALTED.

text.p: Israeli opposition leader Shimon Peres said on Sunday no political force would halt the march of peace in the volatile Middle East region despite the now-threatened peace deals which he helped craft.
Peres, who arrived in South Africa to present President Nelson Mandela with a peacemaker award, said he was confident that the stalled peace process between Israel and Palestine could be revived.

"There is no person or government in our region who can stop the march of history," he told reporters who asked whether the right-wing government of Benjamin Netanyahu posed a threat to a negotiated peace with the Palestinians.

"You can postpone it, you can delay it, you cannot interrupt it. The reasons are so clear and convincing, that it is only a matter of time before the peace process can take its proper course again and all of us will move ahead."

Commenting on Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat's rejection of a new Israeli plan to divide the West Bank town of Hebron into Arab and Jewish parts, which he described as a tragedy and more racist than apartheid South Africa, Peres told Reuters:
"I would not judge Mr Arafat by his pictures. I think we shall overcome the difficulties."

Mandela, who became South Africa's first democratically- elected leader after serving 27 years in jail for his opposition to white rule, declined to comment on Arafat's statement saying: "We have to be very careful in commenting about the person who has been elected by the majority of the people of Israel."
Netanyahu won power in May on a platform to slow peace moves with the Palestinians.

Mandela has twice postponed a planned visit to the Middle East and he said on Sunday that the trip, rescheduled for November, could again be delayed -- this time until January -- due to his slow recovery from recent knee surgery.
"My doctors are very much concerned that the healing process will still be in progress...We'll see, depending on how I feel," he told reporters.

Mandela said the delays did not indicate he was unwilling to visit the region. Instead, he said, he was eager to go in order to encourage Israeli and Palestinian leaders to work towards a negotiated settlement.
"I look forward to this. I will be going to the Middle East as a peace messenger."
